general.title_original: 70-year-old driver escapes as car catches fire outside hospital
general.summary_original:
NAKHON RATCHASIMA — 6 October 2026, A 70-year-old man narrowly escaped after his sedan caught fire and was destroyed outside Sikhio Hospital in Nakhon Ratchasima on Tuesday afternoon.

At around 13:15, Promtham Sikhio rescue workers were alerted to a vehicle fire at the entrance to Sikhio Hospital on Chum Kha Road in Mittraphap subdistrict, Sikhio district.

Rescuers found a silver Toyota Vios with Bangkok license plate กทม 354 Nakhon Ratchasima engulfed in flames, particularly around the engine compartment. Firefighters rushed to control the blaze as people in the area watched.

The car’s owner, identified as 70-year-old Somchai, said he had driven to Nakhon Ratchasima city earlier that morning to see a doctor. The car had been operating normally on his way home until his partner called and asked him to pick her up at Sikhio Hospital.

While waiting at a red light at the Ban Non Kum intersection, he noticed something unusual, which felt like the brakes were sticking. He then smelled smoke and saw it coming from the engine compartment.

Somchai immediately pulled the car onto the roadside near the hospital entrance. Moments later, the vehicle burst into flames. He quickly opened the door and ran to safety.

Two Sikhio Hospital staff members initially tried to help by using fire extinguishers, but they were unable to contain the blaze because the fire was intense and strong winds were blowing.

A fire truck from the Sikhio Municipality disaster prevention and mitigation unit arrived and firefighters sprayed water on the vehicle. The fire was brought under control after about 15 minutes.

Sikhio Mayor Preecha Chantraruwongthong and the deputy mayor visited the scene, while police managed traffic and secured the area.

The cause of the fire remains under investigation.

general.title_original: GULF Strengthens Global LNG Portfolio with New Multi-Year Supply Agreement  with ADNOC
general.summary_original:
Gulf Development Public Company Limited (GULF) today announced the signing of a new multi-year Sales and Purchase Agreement (SPA) with ADNOC, one of the world’s leading energy companies, for the supply of liquefied natural gas (LNG) to strengthen GULF’s global LNG portfolio. The agreement will see ADNOC Trading deliver close to 2 million tonnes of LNG to GULF over a multi-year term, starting in 2027, reinforcing GULF’s strategy to build a diversified and resilient LNG supply chain that anchors its trading business.

The SPA extends a partnership between ADNOC and GULF established through their first LNG supply agreement signed in 2025 and in line with ADNOC’s strategy to expand its presence in the Asian LNG market.

Mr. Sarath Ratanavadi, Chief Executive Officer, Gulf Development Public Company Limited, said: “This agreement reflects the strategic direction we have set for GULF Resources, to build a diversified and resilient LNG portfolio that serves as a strong foundation for our LNG trading business. We have been progressively investing in infrastructure and shipping capabilities, while continuing to expand our relationships with leading global LNG suppliers, strengthening every link across our LNG value chain, from upstream to downstream. This partnership with ADNOC not only enhances the security of our LNG portfolio, but also creates further trading opportunities for GULF in the Asian market. Together with our existing LNG agreements with other partners, it strengthens GULF’s LNG trading capabilities, enabling us to respond to growing energy demand in the future while supporting the region’s energy transition.”

Nasser Al Muhairi, Acting CEO of ADNOC Downstream Industry, Marketing & Trading, said: “This agreement builds on our first LNG supply agreement with Gulf and reinforces ADNOC’s commitment to ensuring reliable energy supplies to our Asian customers. It marks another milestone in ADNOC’s global LNG marketing and trading platform, enhancing the scale, flexibility and optionality of our LNG solutions to meet growing global demand.”
